name: DIGIT

sources.title: M. Lambeta et al., "DIGIT: A Novel Design for a Low-Cost Compact High-Resolution Tactile Sensor with Application to In-Hand Manipulation", IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters, 2020 (arXiv:2005.14679v1)
sources.covers: size, mass, sensing field, image resolution and fps (Table I), camera (OVM7692), USB hub, LEDs

sources.title: digit-interface (the maker's Python interface), Digit.STREAMS at commit 87a28bb (2021-09-22)
sources.covers: stream modes: VGA 640 x 480 at 30 and 15 fps, QVGA 320 x 240 at 60 and 30 fps

note: An open-source optical tactile sensor (design by Meta AI / Facebook AI Research; commercial units are sold by GelSight, whose product page was not read for this entry): a contact sensor, modelled by pad coverage, not a workspace camera, so it has no imagers. From the paper: 20 mm wide x 27 mm high x 18 mm deep (size_mm [18, 20, 27], depth along the camera axis), "approximately 20 g", sensing field 19 x 16 mm, OmniVision OVM7692 colour camera ("a 60 fps color CMOS", focal length 1.15 mm), three RGB LEDs, and a custom PCB with a SuperSpeed USB 3.0 hub. Sources disagree: the paper's Table I gives 640 x 480 at 60 FPS, while the maker's interface library offers VGA (640 x 480) at 30 or 15 fps and QVGA (320 x 240) at 60 or 30 fps; the entry uses the interface's modes (what a user can stream), so tactile.fps is 30 at the 640 x 480 camera_resolution. Stream format and power are not stated. The arXiv v1 PDF was read; the RA-L published version may differ in detail.
